boundary: Exact exported HLSL, entry point, shader model, optimization flags and Edge DXC DLL. All 30 DXIL shader hashes verified against browser output. Browser detailed DXC scopes versus native Compile/GetStatus/GetResult. Serial per-pipeline execution; caches disabled for DXC workload equality. Neither side renders or runs UE. Native is a compiler baseline, not UE editor frame timing. Driver/global caches are retained. Trace is diagnostic. Wall-time remainder after nested shader scopes includes pipeline setup/cache/driver work, not pure driver time.

topic: Exact exported HLSL compile timing in Edge and native Windows, plus DXIL-ready driver samples

hv2021CrossCheck.boundary: Both language modes emit the same shader hashes for these inputs. The dump does not identify the hidden language mode; the timed native baseline uses 2018.

nativeReadyPSO.boundary: Same shader hashes and captured vertex/render/depth/blend/raster/multisample states, compatible diagnostic root signature, not an exact Dawn/UE root signature. CreateGraphicsPipelineState only, DXIL already compiled, no draw submission or visual validation. No global driver cache cleared; first sample is not a guaranteed cold driver. Values are not UE editor timings.

conclusion: Browser and native DXC take comparable time for the identical exported HLSL with identical DXIL shader hashes. Native here is a compiler baseline, not a running UE editor. No measured evidence of a multiple-times browser compiler penalty. Runtime source compilation differs from starting with cooked DXIL. Existing cache-capacity findings are not a new optimization result.
